scenes.headline: How a 1B model finds where a vulnerability lives
scenes.sub: Cisco's Antares: a terminal agent that greps, reads, backtracks and submits.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Glitter! Antares is a family of tiny security models from Cisco. Given a weakness class and a codebase, they find which files hold the flaw. Here's how.

scenes.text: Searching, reading, backtracking and knowing when to stop is a behaviour you can train into a sub-1B model, instead of buying it with scale.
scenes.say: The idea: searching, backtracking and knowing when to stop can be trained into a model under a billion parameters, instead of bought with scale.

steps.say: The model gets only a weakness class and its generic description. No advisory text, no file hints.
It works like an analyst in a terminal, running grep, find and cat against the repo, mounted read-only at its pre-fix commit.

steps.note: 15 terminal calls per task, and no retrieval index
steps.say: It reads the output, reasons, and changes direction when a lead goes cold. The budget is fifteen commands, with no retrieval index.
Then it submits a ranked list of files for a human to look at first. It never patches, and never explains why.

scenes.title: Training, not scale
scenes.say: The same backbone, untrained, scores zero. Everything comes from two stages.

items.text: SFT on security and search traces
items.say: First, supervised fine-tuning on cybersecurity reasoning, deep-research traces and terminal code-search runs.
Then reinforcement learning over full multi-turn trajectories, rewarding correct files, valid submissions, tool-use compliance and exploration.

items.text: It learns to verify and stop
items.say: That second stage teaches it to verify and stop, rather than imitate a trajectory.

scenes.title: File F1 on a 500-task benchmark
scenes.note: a full sweep: $0.71 with Antares-1B, $141 with GPT-5.5
scenes.say: On a new five-hundred-task benchmark, where the best frontier model tops out around point two three, Antares-1B scores point two oh nine, ahead of a seven-hundred-fifty-three-billion-parameter model.

scenes.text: For a narrow, well-shaped task, searching, verifying, backtracking and stopping can be trained into a tiny model.

recap: A terminal agent: grep, read, backtrack, submit
Fifteen commands, no index, a ranked file list
SFT then GRPO; the untrained base scores zero
scenes.say: To recap: a small terminal agent, a tight command budget, and a behaviour that came from training, not size.
